reader.requirement: At --std 85, outside SPECIAL-NAMES, [ALL] HIGH-VALUE(S) is one or more of the character at the highest ordinal position of the PROGRAM collating sequence (native when none is named; under an ALPHABET literal phrase the highest unspecified native character, or the last specified on a tie when every character is specified, §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR5), sized by the associated item; inside SPECIAL-NAMES it is the native highest character (GR7).
reader.edition-search: grep Edition|DialectLevel|Constructs over CollatingModel.cs, FigurativeConstants.cs, SpecialNamesBinder.Alphabets.cs (only the LOCALE arm's DialectLevel<2002 return and the RangeInAlphabet2002 gate, neither on a 1985 literal-phrase path) and the ResolveProgramCollating block of SpecialNamesBinder.cs (no edition switch); the figurativeConstant grammar rule carries no version predicate
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness names every native character (ordinals 1-65536) so it exercises GR5's specified-block arm; the native default, the partly specified alphabet (unspecified characters above), ALL HIGH-VALUE, group and numeric receivers, INSPECT and the SPECIAL-NAMES exception are not exercised

probes.printed: ORD-HV 65536; C1 EQ (X3 VALUE HIGH-VALUE = HIGH-VALUES); C2 GT (> "~"); C5 EQ (group MOVE HIGH-VALUES, ALL HIGH-VALUE); K 01 ORD 65536 (INSPECT REPLACING/TALLYING); C7 EQ (MOVE HIGH-VALUE to PIC 99); MAX 00003
probes.expected: native highest character (implementor's native set: 65,536 UTF-16 units, kb/Work R52)
ALPHABET "B" ALSO "C" "A": 65,535 positions, HIGH-VALUE the highest unspecified character

probes.printed: ORD-HV 65536 ORD-LV 00001; LV IS U+FFFF; HV ABOVE
probes.expected: ALPHABET 65536 "A": U+FFFF lowest, HIGH-VALUE the next native character, highest ordinal
ALPHABET "Z" LOW-VALUE HIGH-VALUE "A": inside SPECIAL-NAMES HIGH-VALUE is the native U+FFFF (position 3), the program's HIGH-VALUE is still the highest position

OK  §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR5  (4.5.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR5

reader.notes: CollatingTable.Extremes computes the highest position over the whole native repertoire (highest unspecified code unit, else GR5's last-specified tie); FigurativeConstants.FillChar reads it from the program alphabet, and AlphabetFigurative pins the SPECIAL-NAMES use to the native extreme. STANDARD-1/STANDARD-2 are treated as the native order, within §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR4 a's implementor correspondence. Classes a, e, f do not bear on the character chosen.

refuter.evidence: Attacks the reader did not try: (1) nested program — 1985 forbids a Configuration Section in a contained program and applies the container's OBJECT-COMPUTER/SPECIAL-NAMES to it; src/hl_nest.cob (ALPHABET "Z" THRU "W" "B" ALSO "C" "A", descending THROUGH) -> inner program ORD-HV 65535 (7 specified chars in 6 positions + 65529 unspecified), HIGH-VALUE > "A" GT: the inner program uses the container's sequence. (2) CLASS clause, a second SPECIAL-NAMES context: src/hl_class.cob (ALPHABET 65536 "A"; CLASS HVC IS HIGH-VALUE) -> program HIGH-VALUE (U+FFFE) is OUT of HVC, the program LOW-VALUE (U+FFFF) is IN: inside SPECIAL-NAMES HIGH-VALUE is the native highest, outside it the program's. (3) src/hl_std1.cob PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE STANDARD-1 -> ORD-HV 65536 (U+FFFF): native characters with no X3.4 correspondence are placed by the implementor (GR4a), so this is latitude, not a defect. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR5; OK §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR7 'When specified as literals in the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, the figurative constants HIGH-VALUE and LOW-VALUE'; OK §1985:VI.4.4.4 GR2; OK §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR1; OK §1985:VI.4.2 'The Configuration Section must not be stated in a program which is contained'; OK §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR4. Side observation (not this rule): hl_std1's IF HIGH-VALUE > "~" only WARNS (COBOL3146) though 1985 VI.6.3.1.1 says 'The relation condition must contain at least one reference to a variable'.
